text:
sophie: heads up — customer AcmeHealth (prod) reports streaming responses dying mid-stream. frontend shows 'broken pipe' and user sees truncated chunks. they say this started after the recent gateway change this morning. escalating because their SLA hit and billing alerts fired.

omar: which endpoint and model? any request ids?

sophie: using /v1/generate-stream (hosted), model=redwood-xl-1, request id from their client: rq_0a9f3c. they sent 10 concurrent streams, ~6 of them aborted after 12–30s. alerting showed ~150 extra 5xx in last 30m. they say it used to be fine.

jamie: @leo can you grab the gateway and runtime logs for rq_0a9f3c? I'm worried client disconnects are being classified as internal 5xx.

leo: digging in. quick notes: our gateway currently maps upstream ECONNRESET / broken pipe to 502 in the metrics pipeline. if the client closed the socket early we should classify as 499 / client abort, not a server 5xx. grabbing logs now.

support-bot: Incident alert created: INC-2026-227-streaming-5xx-spike (priority: P2). Assigned to @leo.

leo: found gateway trace for rq_0a9f3c. snippets below (redacted):

```
[gateway] 2026-03-15T12:08:34Z INFO request_start id=rq_0a9f3c url=/v1/generate-stream client=10.14.2.9
[runtime] 2026-03-15T12:08:46Z ERROR stream_write id=rq_0a9f3c write failed: write tcp 10.1.0.5:443->10.14.2.9:56712: write: broken pipe
[gateway] 2026-03-15T12:08:46Z WARN upstream_closed id=rq_0a9f3c reason=client_reset
[metrics] 2026-03-15T12:08:47Z ERROR classify_response id=rq_0a9f3c status=502 mapped_from=client_reset
```

leo: runtime returned partial chunks, then write to client failed. gateway logged `upstream_closed reason=client_reset` but downstream classification ran a rule that converted all upstream_closed into 5xx for alerting. that mapping is too broad.

omar: do we have a reproducible client? can we make a small script that'll open a streaming request then close after N seconds to reproduce the behavior and see how our metrics count it?

sophie: Acme provided repro steps, pasted from them: they do a streaming SSE-like client with chunked transfer and close after first prompt token arrives. sample curl they gave (they use Node in prod):

```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-xl-1","input":"long prompt...","stream":true}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate-stream
# then client forcibly closes socket after 10--20s
```

jamie: pls add a minimal repro I can run locally. I suspect our gateway should emit 499 and not increment 5xx counters.

leo: I wrote a quick Node repro that opens a streaming request and closes after 15s. ran it against staging and saw the same mapping. logs:

```
client: opened streaming conn, received tokens for ~13s
gateway: write failed: broken pipe
metrics: increment("http.server.errors", {code:502, route:"/v1/generate-stream"})
```

leo: root cause summary (current theory): when the client closes the socket while the server is still streaming, the runtime write error surfaces as EPIPE/ECONNRESET. our gateway currently treats all upstream write failures as internal errors and maps them to 5xx. we need a specific mapping for client aborts -> 499-like metric that does not count as server failure.

omar: does this affect billing? Acme claims they were charged for partial responses.

sophie: billing asked: they saw tokens billed for the request even though the UI showed truncated output. case number BILL-993. From the billing logs: tokens were ingested by runtime and billed. client abort doesn't automatically roll back consumed tokens today.

jamie: so two problems: (1) metrics/alerts are inflated by including client aborts as 5xx; (2) customer-visible confusion about partial streamed output vs billing. short term we should reduce alert noise; long term we should consider marking client-aborted streams separately in billing dashboards.

leo: immediate mitigation idea: change the metrics mapping so that if upstream_closed reason contains "client" or if write error is EPIPE we increment http.server.aborts (499) and NOT http.server.errors(5xx). patch is small in the gateway classifier. I can test on staging.

sophie: customer needs ETA. can we do a hotfix?

leo: I can push a patch to staging in ~30m, run the Node repro, and if good ship to prod with a quick feature flag toggle. rolling to prod would be a 1-line classifier change + small metrics rename; low risk but needs careful rollout so we don't hide real server errors.

jamie: agree. plan: 1) leo deploys classifier toggle to canary (10% traffic), 2) run repros and monitor 5xx vs abort metrics, 3) if stable, ramp to 100% in 15m increments. jamie -> I'll own rollout and rollback.

support-bot: Update INC-2026-227-streaming-5xx-spike: patch proposed, awaiting canary results.

omar: any immediate customer-facing workaround? can Acme change client to wait a bit longer before closing?

sophie: they said closing is by design (they abort if user navigates away). we can tell them we are treating these as client aborts and they won't trigger internal error investigations. they still want confirmation about billing.

leo: for billing, short term — we won't retroactively change charges, but we can flag the account for review and provide a billing credit if we find mis-attribution. long term — add a billing pipeline tag for aborted streams so finance can exclude them from normal compute charges or at least present as partial. that's a product project.

jamie: next steps and owners:
- leo: push classifier change to staging and run repro (ETA 30m)
- jamie: own canary rollout and monitor dashboards (ETA after leo)
- sophie: message Acme with interim note: we're investigating, may reclassify these as client aborts so alerts won't trigger; billing team will review BILL-993. (ETA 1h)
- omar: help validate repro and confirm we see 499 / abort metric in staging

leo: posting the patch snippet I'm about to apply to staging (gateway metrics classification):

```
if (upstream_error.isClientAbort()) {
  metrics.increment('http.server.aborts', {route}); // 499-like
} else {
  metrics.increment('http.server.errors', {code: mapHttpCode(err), route});
}
```

leo: `isClientAbort()` heuristics: treat EPIPE, ECONNRESET on write, or upstream closed with 'client_reset' tag as client abort. we already surface that reason in the trace.

sophie: nice. please add a note in the incident doc about the billing ticket and link BILL-993.

infra-bot: deploy queued: gateway-classifier-staging (build 2026.3.15-482) -> canary group A.

leo: deployed to staging, ran repro script 5x. staging metrics show `http.server.aborts` increments and 5xx count remains flat. logs show EPIPE mapped to abort.

omar: running a load test now to ensure no regression under concurrent aborts. will report in 10m.

jamie: once canary passes, I'll push to prod canary and watch. if aborts are correctly classified we should quiet the alert and close INC-2026-227.

sophie: message to Acme (draft): "We've identified that your client-side aborts were being classified as internal server errors. We're rolling a fix that will classify these as client aborts so they no longer count toward our 5xx SLA alerts. Billing team will review BILL-993 and follow up separately." ok to send?

omar: send it. include repro steps so they understand.

sophie: sent to Acme, they acknowledged and asked for ETA. I told them ~2h for canary + assessment.

support-bot: INC-2026-227 updated: canary successful on staging, prod canary in progress.

leo: prod canary 10% live. initial telemetry looks good: 5xx down to baseline, abort metric bumped on streaming routes. will continue ramping.

jamie: monitor for 30m then ramp to 100% if stable.

sophie: thanks all — closing loop once billing has posted a resolution.

leo: final note for runbook: distinguish client aborts from runtime errors at metrics classification layer; add integration test to ensure aborted streams don't increment 5xx. I'll open a follow-up PR for tests.

omar: adding follow-up ticket: RUNTIME-1258 "classify streaming client aborts as 499 and annotate billing".

support-bot: INC-2026-227 resolved (postmortem pending).
